thread:
kate_support: Hey team — customer (acct: redwood-enterprise-42) reports repeated high latency and 502 spikes since 08:10 UTC. They say the Console shows their endpoint served from eu-west-1 but request traces in their app show responses coming from us-east-1 which adds ~120ms. They attached a couple of request IDs. Can we triage?

customer_john: Confirming — we see the Console region badge = eu-west, but response headers have X-Redwood-Serving-Pop: us-east-1 and our app traces show cross-region hops. This started approx 08:08 UTC after a deploy.

kate_support: Logging for two example request IDs: rqd_01F3A9Y8 (08:09:15) and rqd_01F3B2LQ (08:13:02). Also saw an ops-bot note:

ops-bot: [08:09:16] failover executed for model: gpt-small-v1 -> fallback to us-east-1 (reason: capacity_pressure eu-west-1)

priya_infra: Thanks, forwarding to runtime. Quick checks: can you paste the Console UI session id and the API trace header (x-request-id) for one request? Also did customer use dedicated or hosted?

customer_john: Hosted API. Session id from Console: sess_7e3d. x-request-id: xreq-9a7c. We also captured response headers: 

"x-served-from": "us-east-1",
"x-routing-policy": "preferred=eu-west-1;fallback=us-east-1",
"x-cache-status": "miss"

gavin_runtime: Hmm. ops-bot failover matches. Two things to separate: 1) Why did Console still show eu-west-1 as the serving location? 2) Why did failover happen (capacity) and why wasn't that reflected in real-time console?

maria_analytics: Console display is driven by the customer's configured preferred_region (ui_region) and the control-plane routing map, not the actual serving pop for each request. There is a lag when control-plane cache invalidation fails. We have a TTL for pop mapping of 120s, but if a fallback happens mid-request the Console tile won't update per-request. That could explain visual mismatch but not the cross-region latency itself.

priya_infra: I pulled runtime logs for that timeframe. The routing decision log (node-routing) shows: 

```
2026-03-15T08:09:15Z node-12 route_request id=xreq-9a7c preferred=eu-west-1 selected=us-east-1 reason=capacity_pressure fallback=true
```
This indicates runtime intentionally routed to us-east due to capacity. The anomaly is Console still showing eu-west for that session. Need to confirm whether control-plane did not get the failover event, or if the Console UI is reading stale mapping from the assets cache (cdn).

gavin_runtime: Also noticed that the failover was triggered by a capacity controller event when a small shard OOMed and shifted load. The routing decision is correct. The problem is the Console's per-route metric aggregator only polls per-minute and caches served_pop for quick display. If aggregator had a stuck job at 08:08 it would miss the instant failover.

kate_support: Customer is unhappy because billing/alerting shows requests served in eu-west (lower egress costs) but actual serving in us-east increased their costs. They want a billing reconciliation and assurance this won't happen again.

maria_analytics: For billing, we can provide per-request served_pop by joining request logs with routing decisions. I'll export all request_ids between 08:07-08:15 for acct redwood-enterprise-42. Will need a signed NDA? (customer already has ent contract).

priya_infra: Action items: 1) runtime to attach routing decisions to request logs (done), 2) console team to ensure UI reads per-request served_pop if failover flag set (workaround), 3) ops to inspect capacity controller logs and check why eu-west had pressure.

gavin_runtime: Quick repro suggestion: run a synthetic load to saturate eu-west pool for that account and watch ops-bot failover. Repro steps: 
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Account: redwood-enterprise-42" -d '{"model":"gpt-small-v1","prompt":"hi"}' --repeat 2000 over 2m
- watch node-routing logs for selected pop changes and ops-bot messages

kate_support: Customer asked whether auth or routing bug caused this — they saw a 401 once during the window. Any relation?

priya_infra: 401 likely unrelated — I see a transient IAM token expiration for one client key at 08:11:40. Not correlated with routing failover. We'll give customer timeline: failover at 08:09 due to capacity_pressure; unrelated 401 at 08:11.

customer_john: Appreciate the timeline. Please include headers we can use to verify in future (x-served-from, x-routing-policy, x-fallback-reason). Also we want alerts when routing fallback happens for our account.

maria_analytics: We can add an account-level webhook for fallback events and include served_pop. I'll open a support ticket to provision it; ETA 2d. For short-term, I'll attach the per-request CSV and costs delta to this thread when ready.

ops-bot: [08:20:02] incident-note created id=INC-20260315-0143 linked_to=redwood-enterprise-42

gavin_runtime: Root cause summary I propose: sudden capacity pressure in eu-west pool caused runtime-initiated fallback to us-east. Console UI uses cached per-route served_pop for quick display and did not reflect the instantaneous fallback for that session window. Follow-ups: reduce pop mapping TTL to 30s for control-plane, make Console fall back to per-request served_pop if a recent failover was detected, and add account-level fallback alerts.

kate_support: Thanks — I'm sending interim reply to customer with timeline + next steps. I'll update this thread when we have the CSV and cost reconciliation.

customer_john: Thanks team, we'll hold on the reconciliation but would like a postmortem note once fixes are in place :thumbsup:

priya_infra: Noted. Assigning to runtime/console owners for next week.

kate_support: Closing this support thread for now — moving to incident tracker for follow-ups.
